summary: Looks a string up in a configured key list and outputs the matching mapping — a wirable lookup table with a default.
description: String Mapper compares `inputString` (Input String) against its numbered "input N" entries (displayed Input 0, Input 1, …) using exact string equality. On a match, the `mappedString` (Mapped String) output takes the value of the "output N" entry with the same N (displayed Mapping 0, Mapping 1, … — these mappings are themselves inputs, despite the port name); with no match it takes `defaultMapping` (Default). All values are coerced to strings before comparison, and the mapping re-runs once per update cycle after any of its inputs change. Keys and mappings are usually typed in as parameters but can also be connected.
whenToUse: Use it to translate machine values into display text: status codes to labels, option keys to descriptions, locale keys to phrases. For just true/false use Boolean To String; for composing text with variables inside use String Format; for mappings that live in data rather than in the graph, use an Object or a Function.
runtimeBehavior: Two numbered port series, both inputs, indexed from 0: keys are named "input 0", "input 1", … (group Inputs) and their mapped values are named "output 0", "output 1", … (group Mappings) — pair N maps key N to value N. The editor always offers the next unused index. An authoring tool typically writes both series as parameters (e.g. "input 0": "S", "output 0": "Small"), and may connect any of them.

ports.inputString: String value to look up; compared with strict equality after toString coercion.
ports.defaultMapping: String value used whenever no key matches — also the output before `inputString` first matches anything.
ports.mappedString: String value output: the mapping paired with the matched key, or `defaultMapping`.

patterns: A Radio Button Group's `value` → `inputString`, mappings to human copy → a Text's `text`: option keys stay short and stable while the UI text stays editable in one place.
antiPatterns: Using it for numeric ranges ('0-9' → 'low') — matching is exact equality only; use Expression or Condition chains for ranges.
